chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Aban, from Umar ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi, who said:

Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik sent Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) out from Medina to Syria, and made him stay there. He used to sit with the people in their gatherings. While he was sitting, with a group of people asking him, he looked at the Christians entering into a mountain there. He said: 'What is with these people? Is it their festival today?' They said: 'No, O son of the Messenger of Allah, but they go to a scholar of theirs in this mountain every year on this day, and they bring him out and ask him about what they want and what will happen in their year.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And he has knowledge?' They said: 'He is one of the most knowledgeable of people; he met the companions of the disciples from the companions of Isa (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Shall we go to him?' They said: 'That is up to you, O son of the Messenger of Allah.'

He said: So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) covered his head with his cloth and went with his companions, and they mingled with the people until they came to the mountain. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) sat in the middle of the Christians, he and his companions. The Christians brought out a carpet, then placed the pillows, then entered and brought him out, then tied his eyes. He turned his eyes as if they were the eyes of a snake. Then he turned towards Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Sheikh, are you from us or from the Mercied community?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, from the Mercied community.' He said: 'Are you from their scholars or from their ignorant ones?' He said: 'I am not from their ignorant ones.' The Christian said: 'Shall I ask you or will you ask me?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask me.' The Christian said: 'O group of Christians, a man from the community of Muhammad is saying,

Then he said: 'O servant of Allah, inform me about an hour that is neither from the night nor from the day. Which hour is it?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun.' The Christian said: 'So if it is not from the hours of the night nor from the hours of the day, from which hours is it?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'From the hours of Paradise, and in which our patients are relieved.'

The Christian said: 'Shall I ask you or will you ask me?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask me.' The Christian said: 'O group of Christians, this one is full of answers. Inform me about the inhabitants of Paradise, how they eat but do not excrete? Give me their example in the world.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The unborn in the womb of its mother eats from what its mother eats but does not excrete.' The Christian said: 'Did you not say,

The Christian said: 'Shall I ask you or will you ask me?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ask me.' He said: 'O group of Christians! By Allah, I will ask him about a matter in which he will bog down, just as the donkey bogs down in the mud.' He said to him: 'Ask.' He said: 'Inform me about a man who approached his woman, so she became pregnant with twins, carrying both in one hour, and gave birth to both in one hour, and they both died in one hour, and were buried in one grave. One of them lived for one hundred and fifty years, and the other lived for fifty years. Who were they?' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Uzayr and Uzrat. Their mother became pregnant with them both as you described, and gave birth to both as you described, and Uzayr and Uzrat lived for such and such years. Then Allah, Blessed and High, made Uzayr die for a hundred years, then resurrected him, and he lived with Uzrat for these fifty years, and both of them died in one hour.'

The Christian said: 'O group of Christians, I have not seen with my eyes ever a more knowledgeable one than this man. Do not ask me about a single letter as long as this one is in Syria. Return me.' He said: So they returned him to his cave, and the Christians returned with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What happened between Imam al-Baqir and the Christian scholar in Syria?
ai.summary: This narrative, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the Imam’s intellectual supremacy during his exile under the Umayyad caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik, showcasing his ability to engage with non-Muslim scholars on their own terms. The dialogue serves as a theological demonstration of *'Ilm al-Ladunni* (divine-inspired knowledge), particularly in resolving the Christian community's confusion regarding the lifespan of Uzayr (Ezra) and the nature of the 'hour between night and day.' The Imam’s precise answers not only validated his scholarly authority but also facilitated the conversion or affirmation of faith of the Christian scholar, illustrating the universal applicability of Imami knowledge.
